title: Quad Semiconductor Supply Chain Initiative
implementation: The partners launched joint capacity mapping and vulnerability identification, and later official statements continued to identify the initiative as an active element of Quad semiconductor cooperation.
detail: A four-country initiative to map semiconductor capacity, identify vulnerabilities, and strengthen supply-chain security.

title: U.S.–EU Trade and Technology Council semiconductor partnership
implementation: TTC working groups established cooperation on semiconductor supply-chain transparency, capacity mapping, and policy coordination.
detail: A transatlantic framework for semiconductor supply security, transparency, design, and production capacity.

title: U.S.–Singapore Partnership for Growth and Innovation
implementation: The partnership established an advanced-manufacturing and supply-chain-resilience pillar, identified semiconductor resilience as a concrete bilateral priority, and proceeded through recurring annual dialogues and work programs.
detail: A bilateral economic platform with explicit cooperation on semiconductor supply-chain resilience, advanced manufacturing, standards, and investment.

title: U.S.–Taiwan Technology Trade and Investment Collaboration
implementation: The framework was followed by an April 2022 government-industry forum on U.S.–Taiwan cooperation for global semiconductor supply-chain resilience.
detail: A technology, trade, and investment framework covering semiconductors and other critical supply chains.

title: Japan–U.S. Commercial and Industrial Partnership semiconductor cooperation
implementation: The partners adopted basic principles for semiconductor cooperation in 2022 and continued the work through recurring JUCIP ministerials, a next-generation semiconductor task force, research coordination, and supply-chain consultations.
detail: An operating bilateral framework for semiconductor supply-chain resilience, next-generation research, policy coordination, and technology protection.

title: U.S.–Malaysia Memorandum of Cooperation on Semiconductor Supply Chain Resilience
implementation: The memorandum established government and industry exchanges on transparency, trust, investment, security, and sustainability.
detail: Bilateral cooperation on semiconductor supply-chain resilience and sustainable growth.

title: EU–Japan Digital Partnership
implementation: The partnership has held recurring Digital Partnership Councils and semiconductor policy dialogues through 2026.
detail: A broad digital partnership with continuing work on semiconductors and related technologies.

title: U.S.–Korea Supply Chain and Commercial Dialogue
implementation: Recurring ministerial meetings, working groups, and a semiconductor forum have advanced cooperation on investment incentives, R&D, advanced packaging, materials, workforce development, export controls, and supply-chain risks.
detail: An operating bilateral dialogue with a dedicated semiconductor cooperation agenda and recurring public-private activity.

title: NSF–NSTC Advanced Chip Engineering Design and Fabrication (ACED Fab)
implementation: The U.S. National Science Foundation and Taiwan’s National Science and Technology Council launched ACED Fab under an AIT–TECRO memorandum and implementing arrangement on advanced semiconductor chip design and fabrication. In June 2023, the partnership announced six jointly supported projects using advanced processes available in Taiwan’s semiconductor foundries.
funding: US$6 million total for six joint projects announced in 2023, including US$3 million from NSF for U.S. researchers.
detail: A jointly funded semiconductor research program connecting U.S. chip-design research with advanced fabrication access in Taiwan.

title: Australia–Japan semiconductor supply-chain cooperation
implementation: The Australia–Japan Leaders’ Meeting Joint Statement committed the two governments to explore further opportunities to build stronger and more resilient supply chains, explicitly including semiconductors, within their wider economic-security cooperation.
detail: A bilateral economic-security commitment that identifies semiconductor supply-chain resilience as an explicit cooperation area.

title: EU–Republic of Korea Digital Partnership
implementation: The digital partnership produced four jointly funded semiconductor projects on heterogeneous integration and neuromorphic computing, with continuing cooperation through the EU–Republic of Korea Digital Partnership.
funding: Approximately EUR 12 million total public investment, split equally between the EU and the National Research Foundation of Korea.
detail: A broad digital partnership with an explicit semiconductor cooperation component.

title: EU–Singapore Digital Partnership
implementation: The partnership has held recurring Digital Partnership Council meetings and has pursued collaborative semiconductor research and cross-border investment cooperation.
detail: A broad digital partnership that identifies semiconductors as a priority area for policy, research, and investment cooperation.

title: U.S.–India Semiconductor Supply Chain and Innovation Partnership
implementation: The two governments continued work under the memorandum, and industry associations completed a semiconductor readiness assessment in 2024.
detail: A semiconductor-specific memorandum covering resiliency, innovation, commercial opportunities, and talent.

title: Taiwan–Germany Scientific and Technological Cooperation Arrangement
implementation: Taiwan and Germany signed their first Scientific and Technological Cooperation Arrangement with semiconductors, hydrogen, batteries, and AI as designated cooperation fields. Follow-on activity included a bilateral semiconductor seminar in Dresden and co-funding for six Taiwan–Germany chip-design research teams.
funding: The official sources confirm joint funding for six chip-design research teams but do not state an aggregate amount.
detail: A bilateral science and technology arrangement with an implemented semiconductor research track. Germany is represented through the EU anchor on the map.

title: UK–Japan Semiconductors Partnership
implementation: The 2023 semiconductor partnership produced policy exchanges, research activity, skills cooperation, and industry engagement. In June 2026 the wider UK–Japan Frontier Technology Partnership committed the countries to interlock their AI-semiconductor strengths, while the UK Semiconductor Centre and Rapidus launched a formal pathway connecting UK semiconductor firms with advanced Japanese manufacturing.
funding: UKRI committed GBP 3.99 million, matched by the Japan Science and Technology Agency, for the joint research call.
detail: Joint research, skills, infrastructure access, industry dialogue, and supply-chain resilience.

title: North American Semiconductor Conference and ministerial cooperation
implementation: The three governments committed to biannual official dialogues and cooperation with industry and academia on R&D, workforce, manufacturing, and packaging.
detail: A trilateral framework for research, workforce, investment, manufacturing, and packaging cooperation.

title: U.S.–UK Atlantic Declaration semiconductor cooperation
implementation: The two governments established recurring implementation meetings and began work under the declaration’s technology, investment, economic-security, and resilient-supply-chain pillars.
detail: A broad economic-security framework with explicit cooperation on advanced semiconductor research, compound semiconductors, talent, investment, and supply-chain resilience.

title: EU–Japan Memorandum of Cooperation on Semiconductors
implementation: The memorandum created cooperation on semiconductor R&D, supply-chain early warning, and skills. At the May 2026 Digital Partnership Council, the EU and Japan confirmed implementation of the semiconductor memorandum and continued use of the Early Warning Mechanism to anticipate and mitigate geopolitical or natural supply disruptions.
detail: A semiconductor-specific instrument nested within the EU–Japan Digital Partnership.

title: India–France Horizon 2047 strategic technology cooperation
implementation: The Horizon 2047 roadmap identified semiconductors among the future-oriented sectors for deeper bilateral cooperation, alongside artificial intelligence, digital technology, and other strategic technologies. The roadmap remains subject to recurring leaders’ review.
detail: A long-term strategic roadmap that explicitly identifies semiconductor cooperation as a bilateral priority.

title: Japan–UAE Semiconductor and Battery Cooperation
implementation: The consultation framework was created to identify semiconductor projects and facilitate UAE investment in Japan.
detail: A consultation framework for semiconductor projects and investment alongside battery cooperation.

title: Japan–India Semiconductor Supply Chain Partnership
implementation: Subsequent ministerial meetings reviewed progress and continued company, personnel, and supply-chain cooperation under the partnership.
detail: A policy framework for supply-chain resilience and private-sector cooperation.

title: U.S.–Vietnam Semiconductor Ecosystem Cooperation
implementation: The bilateral memorandum allocated CHIPS Act International Technology Security and Innovation Fund resources to semiconductor workforce development in Vietnam.
funding: USD 2 million from the International Technology Security and Innovation Fund for semiconductor workforce development, alongside separate U.S. STEM education and training support.
detail: A semiconductor ecosystem memorandum centered on workforce development and wider bilateral ecosystem cooperation.

title: Japan–Canada Memorandum of Cooperation on Industrial Science and Technology
implementation: The two governments held the first Industrial Research and Development Policy Dialogue in February 2026 under the memorandum and continued policy exchanges in its priority technology fields.
detail: An industrial science and technology framework that explicitly includes semiconductors among six priority areas for bilateral collaboration.

title: UK–Taiwan Enhanced Trade Partnership semiconductor cooperation
implementation: The Enhanced Trade Partnership was formalized during the annual UK–Taiwan trade talks, where semiconductors were identified as a critical sector for continuing collaboration, trade, and investment.
detail: A formal trade framework with an explicit semiconductor cooperation component.

title: EU–India Memorandum of Understanding on Semiconductor Ecosystems
implementation: The EU–India Trade and Technology Council continued work under the semiconductor memorandum. At its July 2026 meeting, both sides agreed to step up cooperation on semiconductors alongside high-performance computing, quantum technologies, AI, and 6G.
detail: Government-to-government and business cooperation on semiconductor ecosystems, supply chains, and innovation.

title: UK–Republic of Korea Framework for Semiconductor Cooperation
implementation: A UK semiconductor delegation visited the Republic of Korea in February 2025 to develop joint R&D and commercial links under the framework.
detail: A bilateral framework for R&D, skills, industry links, and supply-chain cooperation.

title: UK–Republic of Korea Digital Partnership semiconductor cooperation
implementation: The Digital Partnership created a ministerial forum and a semiconductor cooperation pillar covering R&D in chip design, compound and advanced materials, and advanced packaging. By 2025 the forum was recurring and the two sides had held a Semiconductor Stakeholder Forum in Seoul.
detail: A digital-policy framework separate from the semiconductor-specific UK–Korea framework signed the same day, with its own DSIT–MSIT governance mechanism.

title: Taiwan–France Science and Technology Cooperation Convention
implementation: Taiwan and France signed a Science and Technology Cooperation Convention identifying semiconductors and quantum as one of six priority fields. The framework moved into implementation with the first Taiwan–France Science Research Meeting in April 2024, including semiconductor cooperation among the designated fields.
detail: A bilateral science and technology framework with semiconductors as a formal priority area. France is represented through the EU anchor on the map.

title: EU–Canada Digital Partnership
implementation: The partnership moved into implementation through official-level digital dialogues and held its first Digital Partnership Council in December 2025, with semiconductors retained as a priority.
detail: A broad digital partnership covering semiconductor supply chains, research, innovation, and technology-sector investment.

title: Netherlands–Republic of Korea Semiconductor Alliance
implementation: Government consultations, trade missions, trade-show participation, R&D links, and a bilateral talent program have followed the 2023 alliance.
detail: Government, business, university, and workforce cooperation in the semiconductor sector.

title: Canada–UK Scientific Research and Innovation Memorandum of Understanding
implementation: Canada and the United Kingdom renewed their science, technology, and innovation memorandum with semiconductors named as a priority technology area. The framework subsequently supported a bilateral semiconductor collaborative industrial R&D competition.
funding: No semiconductor-specific amount was specified in the 2024 memorandum.
detail: A ten-year bilateral science and innovation framework that explicitly includes semiconductors and later produced semiconductor-specific collaborative R&D activity.

title: IPEF Supply Chain Agreement
implementation: The agreement entered into force and its institutional bodies began meeting; a semiconductor action-plan team and exercises were subsequently established.
detail: A multilateral supply-chain resilience framework that can cover semiconductor disruptions but is not limited to semiconductors.

title: G7 Semiconductors Point of Contact Group
implementation: The G7 established a semiconductor point-of-contact group for information exchange, research priorities, sustainable manufacturing, non-market practices, and crisis coordination. Subsequent ministerial declarations continued the group and expanded work on trustworthy supply chains, investment frameworks, and cross-border research coordination.
detail: A continuing G7 semiconductor coordination mechanism. France, Germany, and Italy are represented through the EU anchor on the map.

title: U.S.–Uruguay Memorandum of Understanding on Select Critical and Emerging Technologies
implementation: The memorandum establishes a bilateral working group intended to meet twice annually and develop cooperation on semiconductors and other critical technologies. No semiconductor-specific implemented project is documented in the cited source.
detail: Government-level MoU explicitly including semiconductor development and supply-chain opportunities. Uruguay has no country map anchor in the current visualization.

title: Taiwan–Canada Science, Technology and Innovation Arrangement
implementation: Taiwan and Canada signed a Science, Technology and Innovation Arrangement to support priority research, emerging technologies, and talent development. Under the arrangement, the first Joint Science and Technology Committee met in March 2025 and discussed semiconductor, AI, cybersecurity, and talent cooperation.
funding: Not specified in the parent arrangement.
detail: The government-level framework that supports later Taiwan–Canada semiconductor and AI research cooperation.

title: Taiwan–Australia Science and Technology Arrangement
implementation: Taiwan and Australia upgraded their earlier research memorandum to a Science and Technology Arrangement. The agreement identifies ICT manufacturing, semiconductor technology and critical-technology supply-chain resilience as one of four principal cooperation areas.
detail: A bilateral science and technology framework that explicitly links semiconductor cooperation with critical-technology supply-chain resilience.

title: Japan–Republic of Korea–United States Commerce and Industry Ministerial
implementation: The inaugural ministerial established a trilateral mechanism and committed the three governments to accelerate cooperation on resilient semiconductor supply chains, advanced-technology export controls, research, and economic security.
detail: A trilateral commerce and industry mechanism with an explicit semiconductor supply-chain and technology-security agenda.

title: UK–India Technology Security Initiative semiconductor partnership
implementation: The initiative established government coordination and recurring review mechanisms for a broad semiconductor partnership involving research, chip design and IP, compound semiconductors, advanced packaging, workforce, trade missions, manufacturing links, and supply-chain resilience.
funding: Not specified for the semiconductor pillar
detail: A broader technology-security initiative with a detailed semiconductor cooperation pillar spanning research, firms, skills, trade, and manufacturing supply chains.

title: India–Singapore Semiconductor Ecosystem Partnership
implementation: The memorandum links Singapore firms and supply chains with India’s semiconductor ecosystem and supports policy exchange, workforce, and business cooperation.
detail: An ecosystem partnership connecting firms, supply chains, workforce development, and policy exchange.

title: Quad Semiconductor Supply Chains Contingency Network
implementation: Quad leaders welcomed a Memorandum of Cooperation establishing a Semiconductor Supply Chains Contingency Network to improve preparedness and continuity when semiconductor supply chains are disrupted.
detail: A four-country contingency framework focused on semiconductor supply-chain preparedness and resilience.

title: JETRO–NY CREATES Strategic Semiconductor Partnership MoU
implementation: The parties signed a semiconductor-sector MoU and subsequently co-hosted a SEMICON Japan seminar. JETRO also reports continuing business development activities under the partnership.
detail: Public trade agency and U.S. nonprofit research-organization partnership for cross-border semiconductor R&D and ecosystem connections.

title: France–UAE Framework Agreement on Artificial Intelligence
implementation: The framework provides for a one-gigawatt AI campus in France and broader collaboration across the AI value chain, explicitly including acquisition of advanced chips, data centers, talent, sovereign cloud, and cross-border investment.
funding: Investment volume was not specified in the framework announcement; a first investment tranche was scheduled for a later announcement.
detail: A bilateral AI infrastructure and investment framework with an explicit advanced-chip component.

title: U.S.–India TRUST critical and emerging technology initiative
implementation: The leaders launched TRUST to promote government, academic, and private-sector collaboration in critical technologies, including semiconductors, and committed to trusted and resilient semiconductor, critical-mineral, and advanced-material supply chains.
detail: A trusted-technology initiative covering semiconductor collaboration, investment, vendor security, and resilient supply chains.

title: European Semicon Coalition
implementation: Nine EU governments launched the Semicon Coalition in March 2025 to coordinate semiconductor production capacity, research, commercialization, and workforce development. By September 2025, all 27 EU member states had signed the coalition declaration, which also prioritizes investment, sustainability, and international partnerships.
funding: No coalition-specific funding amount was announced. The launch statement noted EUR 43 billion available for the European semiconductor industry through the EU Chips Act.
detail: A semiconductor-specific member-state coordination mechanism. The Netherlands is shown as the initiating mapped hub and the EU node represents the wider coalition.

title: Singapore–Vietnam Comprehensive Strategic Partnership
implementation: The partnership committed the two countries to education, professional exchange, and talent development in integrated-circuit design and semiconductor technology. A subsequent plan of action and 2026 bilateral initiatives continued implementation.
detail: A broad strategic partnership with an explicit semiconductor-design and skills component.

title: India–Malaysia structured semiconductor cooperation initiative
implementation: 2025 officials announced structured semiconductor engagement. A February 2026 leaders statement documented cooperation already underway between IIT-Madras Global and Malaysia Advanced Semiconductor Academy, and between IESA and MSIA. These institutional initiatives do not by themselves establish a separately signed bilateral government semiconductor agreement.
detail: An announced bilateral cooperation process intended to connect Malaysia’s established supply chain with India’s expanding semiconductor ecosystem.

title: Vietnam–Japan semiconductor research cooperation
implementation: Five joint semiconductor research projects were launched in 2026, covering three-dimensional integrated circuits, advanced transistor materials, sensors, secure RISC-V systems-on-chip, and wide-bandgap power electronics. The partners also targeted additional co-funded projects.
funding: Implemented under Japan’s NEXUS program for ASEAN, reported with an estimated program budget of USD 100 million for 2024–2029; the full amount is not dedicated solely to these projects.
detail: Government-backed cooperation connecting Vietnamese and Japanese research institutions in semiconductor materials, design, devices, and manufacturing technologies.

title: U.S.–UAE AI Acceleration Partnership
implementation: The framework established a joint implementation and monitoring group and a pathway for protected advanced-technology cooperation, including a one-gigawatt data center within a planned five-gigawatt AI technology cluster.
funding: No public funding figure specified; the framework describes a planned 5 GW UAE–U.S. AI technology cluster and associated cross-border investment.
detail: A trusted-technology framework linking access to advanced AI semiconductors and infrastructure with security commitments, monitoring, and Emirati investment.

title: Singapore EDB–Brabant Development Agency Deep Technology MoU
implementation: The public agencies agreed to support knowledge and policy exchange, talent initiatives and joint research opportunities. Semiconductors and photonics are explicit deep-tech cooperation fields.
detail: Public development-agency agreement with an explicit semiconductor cooperation component.

title: Taiwan–Israel semiconductor design and next-generation materials research program
implementation: Taiwan’s National Science and Technology Council issued a bilateral Taiwan–Israel add-on research call focused on semiconductor design and next-generation materials. The public call set a project period from January 2026 through December 2027; the source confirms the bilateral program but does not identify awardees.
funding: Not specified in the public call page.
detail: A bilateral research program narrowly focused on semiconductor design and next-generation materials.

title: Australia–Vietnam Strategic Technologies Centre
implementation: The Australian and Vietnamese governments established the Strategic Technologies Centre through Vietnam’s Posts and Telecommunications Institute of Technology and the University of Technology Sydney. The centre was launched in Hanoi to support research, policy, and industry collaboration in semiconductors, AI, 5G/6G, and cybersecurity.
funding: Australia’s Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade provided AUD 2.1 million in initial funding to establish the centre.
detail: A government-backed operating research centre covering several strategic technologies, with semiconductors explicitly included.

title: Canada–UK compound-semiconductor supply-chain partnership
implementation: The three-year memorandum was followed by a Canada–UK collaborative industrial R&D call in compound semiconductors.
detail: Institutional cooperation on compound-semiconductor photonics, commercialization, and resilient G7 supply chains.

title: Japan–India Digital Partnership 2.0
implementation: The updated Digital Partnership makes semiconductors a designated cooperation domain. It calls for deeper links between semiconductor R&D institutions, promotion of bilateral semiconductor investment, and stronger semiconductor supply-chain resilience.
detail: A broader digital partnership with a defined semiconductor ecosystem pillar alongside AI, digital public infrastructure, firms, startups, and talent.

title: JETRO–TAITRA–Kyushu Economic Federation Investment Cooperation MoC
implementation: The memorandum promotes Taiwanese semiconductor-related investment in Kyushu through investment missions, information sharing, matchmaking and establishment support.
detail: Three-party agency and industry-federation agreement supporting semiconductor supply-chain investment.

title: Malaysia–Netherlands Memorandum of Cooperation on Semiconductor Industry
implementation: The memorandum created an Annual Bilateral Semiconductor Dialogue to review initiatives and coordinate policy exchange, talent development, research and development, and technology sharing.
detail: A semiconductor-specific framework combining Malaysia’s packaging and testing base with Dutch equipment, manufacturing, and innovation capabilities.

title: UK–Taiwan Semiconductor Joint Skills Project
implementation: The two sides signed a government-supported memorandum to establish semiconductor talent cooperation. The first program was completed in March 2026, bringing UK semiconductor students and researchers into Taiwan’s university and industry ecosystem.
funding: Program support included funding from the UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology; a total public amount was not specified in the cited source.
detail: A bilateral semiconductor skills mechanism that moved from memorandum to an implemented exchange program within six months.

title: U.S.–UK Technology Prosperity Deal MoU
implementation: The government MoU commits to cooperation on AI infrastructure and hardware innovation and promotion of AI exports including chips, data centers and models. No chip-specific downstream project is confirmed in this document.
detail: Cross-government technology memorandum explicitly covering chips and AI hardware.

title: U.S.–Japan Technology Prosperity Deal MoC
implementation: The memorandum commits to cooperation in high-performance computing, leading-edge semiconductor technologies, quantum computing and research across strategic science fields. It is distinct from earlier JUCIP semiconductor cooperation.
detail: Cross-government MoC specifically mentioning leading-edge semiconductor technologies.

title: UK–Netherlands Innovation Partnership semiconductor cooperation
implementation: The Innovation Partnership identifies semiconductors, artificial intelligence, and quantum as initial cooperation areas and establishes work plans and a governance structure for continuing bilateral science, innovation, and technology cooperation.
detail: A bilateral innovation framework in which semiconductor cooperation is an explicit priority alongside AI and quantum technologies.

title: Korea–UAE cooperation framework on AI and semiconductors
implementation: The joint declaration committed the two governments to explore concrete projects involving joint investment, development, exports, AI data centers, technology exchange, and stable supply chains for core materials.
detail: A future-oriented strategic framework that explicitly connects AI infrastructure and semiconductor cooperation with joint investment and technology development.

title: U.S.–Saudi Strategic Artificial Intelligence Partnership
implementation: The partnership covers the supply of advanced semiconductors, development of AI applications and infrastructure, national capability building, and high-value bilateral investment.
detail: A government-to-government AI framework in which access to advanced semiconductors supports Saudi compute infrastructure, capability development, and investment cooperation.

title: India–Netherlands Partnership on Semiconductors and Related Emerging Technologies
implementation: Official 2026 statements report links between competence centers, an online semiconductor school, university partnerships, and firm participation.
detail: Cooperation linking the Dutch semiconductor ecosystem with India’s mission, universities, and industry.

title: Pax Silica Declaration
participants: Australia;Israel;Japan;South Korea;Singapore;United Kingdom;United States;European Union;United Arab Emirates;India;Netherlands
implementation: The declaration established trusted-technology cooperation across semiconductors, compute, advanced manufacturing, critical inputs, infrastructure, and investment security. Membership expanded during 2026, including the United Arab Emirates in January, India in February, the European Union in June, and the Netherlands by July.
detail: A broad trusted-technology framework with explicit semiconductor, compute, advanced-manufacturing, and critical-mineral components.

title: India–Germany Semiconductor Ecosystem Partnership
implementation: India and Germany signed a Joint Declaration of Intent on a Semiconductor Ecosystem Partnership. The leaders described the mechanism as an institutional dialogue across the semiconductor value chain intended to deepen research and industrial collaboration between the two ecosystems.
detail: A semiconductor-specific bilateral framework. Germany is represented through the EU anchor on the map.

title: Taiwan–Japan NSTC–RIKEN semiconductor research program
implementation: Taiwan’s NSTC and Japan’s RIKEN approved bilateral research projects for 2026–2028 under their standing cooperation arrangement. Next-generation compound semiconductors are one of the designated joint research fields, and funded projects began on April 1, 2026.
funding: Public award notice confirms funded projects but does not state the aggregate semiconductor allocation.
detail: An operating bilateral research program under the NSTC–RIKEN framework with next-generation compound semiconductors as a designated field.

title: U.S.–Taiwan Agreement on Semiconductor Trade and Investment
implementation: AIT and TECRO signed an agreement linking semiconductor investment commitments, industrial clusters, supply-chain expansion, and U.S. treatment of Taiwan under semiconductor-related trade measures.
funding: At least USD 250 billion in new direct investment commitments by Taiwanese semiconductor and technology enterprises, with at least USD 250 billion in credit guarantees described by the official fact sheet.
detail: A large bilateral trade-and-investment arrangement focused on expanding semiconductor production and supply-chain capacity in the United States.

title: Canada–Taiwan joint semiconductor and AI research program
implementation: NSERC and Taiwan’s NSTC launched a joint research program covering AI-enabled semiconductor design, manufacturing and packaging, compound semiconductors for AI, and MEMS sensors. The full-proposal stage closed on July 30, 2026, with joint funding decisions pending.
funding: NSERC and NSTC each committed up to C$1 million, with up to C$225,000 per three-year project and approximately four awards planned.
detail: A jointly funded agency-level research program connecting Canadian AI strengths with Taiwan’s semiconductor expertise.

title: EU–Vietnam Comprehensive Strategic Partnership semiconductor cooperation
implementation: The EU and Vietnam upgraded their relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and explicitly identified semiconductors, resilient and diversified supply chains, secure digital connectivity, and semiconductor supply chains as areas for deeper cooperation.
detail: A broad strategic partnership with explicit semiconductor supply-chain and digital-connectivity cooperation.

title: India–U.S. AI Opportunity Partnership
implementation: India and the United States signed the AI Opportunity Partnership as a bilateral addendum to the Pax Silica Declaration. The partnership focuses on the physical AI stack, joint R&D, next-generation data-center investment, access to compute and advanced processors, and trusted technology supply chains.
detail: A bilateral AI and trusted-technology framework linked directly to Pax Silica, whose supply-chain scope includes silicon, semiconductors, advanced computing, and critical inputs.

title: India–Israel Critical and Emerging Technologies initiative
implementation: India and Israel elevated their strategic partnership and launched a National Security Adviser-led initiative on Critical and Emerging Technologies. Their joint statement explicitly commits the two countries to integrate complementary capabilities in semiconductors alongside AI, cybersecurity, quantum, biotechnology, defence technology, and space.
detail: A broad critical-technology initiative with semiconductors explicitly identified as a field for deeper bilateral integration and institutional cooperation.

title: JETRO–Arizona State University–ACA–GPEC Semiconductor Collaboration MoU
implementation: JETRO and three Arizona partner organizations signed a four-party memorandum for R&D, skills and cross-border industrial collaboration in semiconductors and related sectors.
detail: Subnational and institutional semiconductor ecosystem MoU; distinct from U.S.–Japan government agreements.

title: Japan–Singapore Strategic Partnership semiconductor cooperation
implementation: The Strategic Partnership directs officials to deepen semiconductor cooperation, particularly joint research and development on next-generation semiconductor technologies, and places this work within wider economic-security and supply-chain cooperation.
detail: A broad strategic partnership with an explicit next-generation semiconductor R&D component and formal implementation oversight.

title: Joint Israel–Chips Joint Undertaking semiconductor R&D programs
implementation: The 2026 call is open for proposals; awards and final project budgets had not been determined at the verification date.
funding: Up to EUR 3.5 million allocated by the Israel Innovation Authority for approved Israeli participants; allocation does not guarantee awards.
detail: International R&D cooperation for semiconductor technologies through the European Chips Joint Undertaking.

title: India–Singapore industry-led semiconductor corridor
implementation: The Singapore Semiconductor Industry Association and India Cellular and Electronics Association signed a memorandum to build a trusted semiconductor corridor, advance technology co-development, support two-way business collaboration, and conduct a joint ecosystem study.
detail: A government-documented industry association agreement designed to operationalize the broader India–Singapore semiconductor partnership.

title: India–Vietnam Memorandum of Understanding on Digital Technology Cooperation
implementation: The memorandum identifies semiconductor technology, artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, and innovation ecosystems as areas for bilateral cooperation. No completed semiconductor project was documented at the verification date.
detail: A broader digital-technology agreement with an explicit semiconductor component and provisions for technology and innovation cooperation.

title: India–Italy Joint Declaration and INNOVIT India Semiconductor Cooperation
implementation: A government joint declaration announced creation of INNOVIT India for startup, research and industry cooperation across named sectors including semiconductors. A separately signed semiconductor-specific MoU is not established by the declaration.
detail: Government joint declaration identifying semiconductors in a newly announced bilateral innovation hub.

title: Japan–Italy Memorandum of Cooperation on Supply Chain Resilience
implementation: Japan and Italy signed a memorandum to promote and deepen supply-chain resilience cooperation among like-minded partners in areas including semiconductors, critical minerals, and advanced technologies.
detail: A broader economic-security supply-chain agreement with semiconductors as an explicit cooperation field. Italy is represented through the EU anchor on the map.

title: Canada–Germany Joint Declaration of Intent on Semiconductor Cooperation
implementation: The declaration establishes policy dialogue and deeper cooperation on semiconductor investment, industrial development, technology, research, supply-chain resilience, and opportunities for start-ups, scale-ups, and smaller firms.
detail: A bilateral semiconductor framework. Germany is represented through the EU anchor on the map.

title: Australia–Canada–India Technology and Innovation Partnership
implementation: The memorandum provides for a trilateral working group to implement cooperation on AI and other technologies, including semiconductors. Evidence of an actual working-group meeting is not yet identified.
detail: A trilateral technology partnership with semiconductors as an explicit cooperation field and a joint working group responsible for implementation.

title: France–South Korea MoU on AI, Semiconductors and Quantum Technologies
implementation: The governments signed an MoU during the Korean president's visit to France. Official accounts identify AI, semiconductors and quantum technologies as cooperation fields and reference joint R&D and market-access cooperation.
detail: New signed government technology MoU, distinct from the April 2026 letter of intent.

title: Singapore SSIA–Brabant Development Agency Semiconductor MoU
implementation: The industry association and Dutch development agency signed an MoU to support supplier qualification, business matching, skills, investment missions and exchanges between semiconductor ecosystems. It is separate from the May 2025 EDB–BOM MoU.
detail: Industry association–public development agency semiconductor-specific MoU.
